text.arabic_uthmani: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا۟ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَٰنِينَ جَلْدَةًۭ وَلَا تَقْبَلُوا۟ لَهُمْ شَهَٰدَةً أَبَدًۭا ۚ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ

words.gloss_range: opening connector joining this ruling to the preceding legal block while starting a fresh case
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ruling as continuation, not isolation. It binds the false-accusation case to the preceding legal block (24:2-3) while still launching a new relative-clause topic. The first sound of the ayah therefore makes the qadhf rule part of a connected legal sequence before the accusers are named.

topics.headline: connected legal opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ruling enters as a connected legal continuation, not as an isolated maxim.
topics.reason: The connector precedes the class-defining relative phrase and the row set links the ayah to the preceding legal block (24:2-3).

words.gloss_range: definite relative opener defining an open legal class through the full accusation-and-failed-proof condition
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not name a closed group; it makes a repeatable legal class. The class is completed only by the accusation and the failed production of witnesses, then answered by the result clause. This keeps the penalties tied to the full condition rather than to accusation alone.

topics.headline: open class defined by conduct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the penalties attach to whoever fits the described conduct, not to a pre-named historical group.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun heads the condition and waits for the result command, so the class is defined by the following clauses.

words.gloss_range: accuse by a directed throwing image, locally aimed at the protected object and continued in the surah accusation field
words.root_gloss_range: throwing, casting, and by extension accusation; local grammar selects verbal accusation as a directed projectile
words.prose: {{ar:يَرْمُونَ}} ({{tr:yarmūna}}) frames accusation as a directed cast. Its object is the protected women, so the speech act is not neutral talk but a charge aimed at a guarded target. The plural imperfect makes the accusers a repeatable conduct-class rather than one finished incident. The same accusation field returns in the surah (24:6; 24:23), while the battle use at 8:17 remains only a contrast for the root's wider range.

topics.headline: overstated occurrence count
topics.blocking_evidence: Contextual evidence lists six exact-root form instances, so the claim that the root appears only once is not reliable for local interpretation.
topics.reason: The row overstates rarity by relying on an incomplete lexicon count; the local marked accusation frame survives without that claim.

topics.headline: same-surah accusation recurrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this accusation verb belongs to a same-surah legal field, while wider battle usage does not govern the local legal sense.
topics.reason: Rows with 24:6 and 24:23 support same-surah recurrence; 8:17 is useful contrast but does not control the local accusation frame.

topics.headline: plural imperfect conduct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the legal subject is formed by repeatable group conduct rather than a single narrated incident.
topics.reason: The imperfect plural form supplies ongoing or repeatable group agency within the relative construction.

topics.headline: accusation as directed projectile
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation is pictured as something cast at a protected target.
topics.reason: The verb takes the protected women as its object, and the surviving semantic rows converge on a throwing-to-accusing transfer.

words.gloss_range: definite protected feminine plural object, with fortress imagery and standard passive protected status
words.root_gloss_range: fortifying, protecting, enclosing, and chastity-status language; local form names protected women as the target of accusation
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-muḥṣanāti}}) names the target as already protected before the accusation is assessed. The fortress field makes the charge feel like an attempted breach of guarded status, and the standard passive participle presents protection as a standing condition. A variant active-participle reading can shift agency toward self-guarding, but it does not replace the local protected-object role. Since the same protected-status term carries different scopes in 4:24, 4:25, 5:5, and 24:23, this verse's accusation frame controls its local scope.

topics.headline: passive protection with active-reading contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that protection can be viewed as received status or self-guarding agency, while the standard local parse keeps the passive protected state.
topics.reason: The standard form is passive participle; the active-participle variant is valid contrast but cannot replace the canonical local form.

topics.headline: protected enclosure and final exit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah opening with protected enclosure and closing by naming the accusers as boundary-exiters.
topics.reason: The row set links this protected target with the final boundary-exit label, producing a frame across the ayah.

topics.headline: context controls protected-status scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same protected-status term can carry different legal scopes, so this verse must be read from its local accusation frame.
topics.reason: Cross-references to 4:24, 4:25, 5:5, 24:4, and 24:23 show range, but local attachment fixes this word as the object of accusation.

topics.headline: protected object before proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accused class is grammatically protected before the legal demand for proof begins.
topics.reason: The noun is definite, feminine plural, and the direct object of the accusation verb, with protected-status semantics supported by the root evidence.

words.gloss_range: delayed sequence marker separating accusation from later failed proof-production
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) divides the condition into two beats. First comes the accusation; then comes the later failure to produce witnesses. The connector gives the legal process room for proof to be demanded before the result clause arrives.

topics.headline: two-stage condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment follows accusation plus a later proof failure, not accusation by itself.
topics.reason: The particle scopes over the whole failed-production clause and separates it from the accusation stage.

words.gloss_range: past-negating jussive particle making witness non-production a completed legal fact
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) turns the following bringing verb into a completed non-production. The issue is not weak evidence or an attempt still underway; the witnesses were not produced. That closed failure is what lets the consequence particle move into enforcement.

topics.headline: completed absence of proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse treats proof as categorically absent before any penalty begins.
topics.reason: The particle governs the jussive verb and gives the imperfect a past-negated legal value.

words.gloss_range: bring-or-produce verb narrowed by bi-governance into evidentiary production
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, bringing, and producing; local bi-complement selects production of evidence
words.prose: {{ar:يَأْتُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) is narrowed by its complement into producing evidence, not merely arriving. The accusers must bring witnesses into the legal scene, and the jussive form keeps the same group responsible for failing to do so. The demand reappears as a same-surah challenge at 24:13.

topics.headline: jussive failed production by same group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same plural accuser group remains responsible for the failed production.
topics.reason: The jussive plural form is governed by the negating particle while retaining third-person plural subject agreement.

topics.headline: proof demand echoed at 24:13
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demand to bring four witnesses becomes a later rhetorical test in the same surah (24:13).
topics.reason: Rows point to 24:13 as a near-verbatim restatement of the proof-production demand.

topics.headline: coming narrowed to evidence production
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the required act is procedural production of witnesses, not bare arrival.
topics.reason: The verb can mean come broadly, but the local bi-complement and witness phrase select bring or produce as the active sense.

words.gloss_range: preposition binding the witnesses as accompaniment and evidentiary means of the bringing verb
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the small hinge that makes the witnesses accompany the accusers as evidence. It prevents the bringing verb from reading as simple arrival and binds the four-witness phrase into the proof package. The legal demand is therefore to come with proof, not merely to mention proof.

topics.headline: witnesses as brought proof package
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that witnesses must be presented as accompanying evidence, not just named as absent possibilities.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the four-witness phrase as the complement of the production verb.

words.gloss_range: exact fourfold proof threshold governed by the preposition and bound to witnesses
words.root_gloss_range: fourness, quartering, and settled fourfold structure; local use is an exact legal count
words.prose: {{ar:أَرْبَعَةِ}} ({{tr:arbaʿati}}) fixes the proof threshold as four, not an open plural. Its grammar binds the number to the witness noun, and the surah repeats the four-plus-witnessing pattern in related accusation procedures (24:6; 24:8; 24:13). Root imagery of quartered stability can color the threshold, but the local force is exact count.

topics.headline: quartered stability as color, not replacement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a concrete pressure of four-sided stability while keeping the local meaning as the legal number four.
topics.reason: The root family can supply quarter and dwelling imagery, but the local noun remains a cardinal number in the proof threshold.

topics.headline: four and witnessing pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that fourfold proof structures accusation law across the surah, with distinct mechanisms at 24:6, 24:8, and 24:13.
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete same-surah references where four and witnessing recur in related legal frames.

topics.headline: fixed four-witness count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that legal proof is set by an exact fourfold threshold rather than by a vague demand for witnesses.
topics.reason: The number is genitive after the preposition and heads the witness-count phrase.

words.gloss_range: plural witness-agents required as present attestors, with case-variant pressure around the counted phrase
words.root_gloss_range: presence, witnessing, testimony, and attestation; local noun names witness-persons rather than abstract testimony
words.prose: {{ar:شُهَدَآءَ}} ({{tr:shuhadāʾa}}) names witness-persons, not an abstract proof idea. The root points first to presence and perception, so the demanded agents must be direct attestors. A variant parse can make the witness noun a specification rather than the standard bound count, but both readings preserve the four-witness threshold; the later testimony noun then turns the missing agents into lost capacity.

topics.headline: martyr sense not locally active
topics.blocking_evidence: The local syntax requires legal witness-agents governed by the four-count phrase, and no evidence makes martyrdom the active sense here.
topics.reason: The broader polysemy is real lexically, but the local legal proof frame blocks treating martyrdom as an active payoff.

topics.headline: sound closure adds no separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The audible-closure point repeats the already retained proof-package closure without adding a distinct lexical or structural payoff.
topics.reason: The row is decorative after the witness-agent and phrase-architecture topics have been retained.

topics.headline: case variant tests phrase architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase can be grammatically tested without changing the legal threshold.
topics.reason: The standard reading binds the witness noun to the number, while the tanwin variant reparses it as specification; both retain four witnesses.

topics.headline: agent witness becomes testimony loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same witness root moves from required agents to the testimony the accusers later lose.
topics.reason: The row set links this witness-agent noun with the later testimony noun, making requirement and sanction mirror each other.

topics.headline: present witness-persons required
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof demand requires persons who can attest from presence, not reputation or rumor.
topics.reason: The broken plural noun denotes witness-agents governed by the four-count phrase.

words.gloss_range: result particle turning the completed condition into the legal consequence clause
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge from condition to enforcement. It makes the command answer accusation plus failed proof, so the first penalty is not detached from the evidentiary failure. The result force moves the ayah from legal description into binding command.

topics.headline: condition answered by consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the flogging command is caused by the completed condition, not presented as an isolated command.
topics.reason: The result particle introduces the apodosis after the failed proof-production clause.

words.gloss_range: imperative flogging command with attached object pronoun, direct action, and same-surah penalty echo
words.root_gloss_range: skin, flogging, striking the skin, and endurance-related derivatives; local command selects direct flogging as bounded bodily penalty
words.prose: {{ar:ٱجْلِدُوهُمْ}} ({{tr:ijlidūhum}}) shifts from third-person accusers to second-person enforcers. The object suffix carries the same accusers forward without renaming them, and the Form I imperative commands the direct act. The skin-root makes the sanction a bounded surface act, while the later counted unit repeats the same root so the command becomes measurable through its own wording. Its root and form echo the flogging penalty at 24:2, but here the count and cause distinguish false accusation from the offense alleged.

topics.headline: prior-verse transition note
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The brief previous-verse note does not add a distinct reader-facing payoff beyond the retained same-surah legal echo.
topics.reason: It is too underspecified to affect local word prose.

topics.headline: 24:2 penalty echo with changed count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same flogging command links 24:2 and 24:4 while the different count separates the two offenses.
topics.reason: The rows connect this imperative with the same root and command form in 24:2.

topics.headline: command echoed by counted unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act and its counted unit repeat the same root, making the punishment measurable through its own wording.
topics.reason: The command and the later unit share the same root in a cognate punishment frame.

topics.headline: skin-root bodily sanction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sanction is embodied as a bounded surface act, while broader endurance associations remain secondary color.
topics.reason: The skin and flogging branch is locally selected; endurance derivatives may color the family but do not establish a rehabilitation claim.

topics.headline: same accusers carried as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attached pronoun keeps the penalty aimed at the same relative-clause group.
topics.reason: The object suffix is syntactically forced as the imperative object and refers back to the accuser group.

topics.headline: direct command to enforcers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from describing accusers to commanding an enforcing audience.
topics.reason: The verb is a second-person plural imperative with an implicit enforcing subject.

words.gloss_range: accusative fixed number measuring the lash unit and calibrating qadhf penalty within the legal block
words.root_gloss_range: eightness and value or price associations; local use is the exact number eighty as penalty measure
words.prose: {{ar:ثَمَٰنِينَ}} ({{tr:thamānīna}}) fixes the punishment as a measured total. It depends on the following unit word, so eighty is not abstract quantity but eighty lashes. Against the hundred in 24:2, the number calibrates false accusation within the same legal block; value-language in the root family is only secondary color for that calibration.

topics.headline: cadence point adds no separate legal payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The measured-cadence point is already captured by the exact-total and counted-unit topics.
topics.reason: It repeats the retained quantity-to-unit payoff.

topics.headline: value-root color under exact count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a calibration pressure in the root family without losing the local force of the cardinal number.
topics.reason: Price or value associations can color the number, but local grammar selects the fixed number eighty.

topics.headline: calibrated below 24:2 count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that eighty differentiates the false-accusation penalty from the hundred-lash penalty at 24:2.
topics.reason: The row set compares the eighty count here with the one hundred count in 24:2 and treats the number as legally specific.

topics.headline: fixed eighty-lash total
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the penalty is an exact counted total anchored in the following lash unit.
topics.reason: The number functions as the measure of the counted unit.

words.gloss_range: single counted lash unit serving both as cognate accusative and specification of eighty
words.root_gloss_range: skin, lash, flogging-instance, and surface-contact imagery; local noun is a single countable flogging unit
words.prose: {{ar:جَلْدَةًۭ}} ({{tr:jaldatan}}) makes the penalty countable one stroke at a time. It both echoes the flogging command as a cognate unit and specifies what the eighty measures. Because the root is tied to skin and flogging, the legal number remains attached to repeated bodily surface contact rather than becoming an abstract penalty total. The same-surah flogging field links this counted unit with 24:2 while preserving this verse's distinct eighty-count context.

topics.headline: sound and prior-domain notes add no separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound and previous-domain notes do not add a distinct local payoff after countability, skin image, and same-surah penalty echo are retained.
topics.reason: These rows are decorative or underspecified for word prose.

topics.headline: surface contact remains visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that each counted unit remains connected to the skin-root image of bodily surface contact.
topics.reason: The root family supports skin and flogging associations, while local grammar makes the word a single instance noun.

topics.headline: same-surah flogging frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counted unit shares the same-surah flogging field with 24:2 while preserving this verse’s eighty-count context.
topics.reason: The row links the cognate punishment frame here with the 24:2 flogging context.

topics.headline: single lash as counted unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment is bounded as eighty discrete instances of the same act named by the command.
topics.reason: The noun functions as counted unit and cognate reinforcement for the flogging command.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector adding the testimony ban as a second cumulative sanction
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds a second penalty rather than offering an alternative to flogging. It coordinates the whole no-acceptance clause, extending the legal consequence from bodily punishment to testimonial capacity. The penalty sequence accumulates: body, legal speech, then identity verdict.

topics.headline: testimony ban added to flogging
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that testimony rejection is a cumulative co-penalty, not a substitute for flogging.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the full prohibition clause with the preceding imperative penalty.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle governing the acceptance verb as a binding command of non-acceptance
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) makes the next verb a prohibition, not a prediction. The addressed authority is commanded not to accept testimony from the accusers. With the later time adverb, the refusal is stretched beyond the original case inside this ayah.

topics.headline: commanded non-acceptance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the testimony clause is a binding prohibition on acceptance, not merely a report of non-acceptance.
topics.reason: The particle governs the jussive acceptance verb and the clause is extended by the time adverb.

words.gloss_range: acceptance verb in a legal validation frame with testimony as object and the accusers as affected source
words.root_gloss_range: receiving, accepting, turning toward, and facing; local Form I selects legal admissibility or reception
words.prose: {{ar:تَقْبَلُوا۟}} ({{tr:taqbalū}}) moves the sanction into legal validation. It takes testimony as object and the accusers as the party whose speech is refused. The facing-orientation branch gives the refusal a concrete feel of turning away from their testimony, while the local Form I keeps the issue at admissibility rather than gracious approval; 5:27 remains a contrast in a different acceptance frame.

topics.headline: prior declaration note adds no separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The brief 24:3 note is too underspecified to add to the local acceptance-prohibition analysis.
topics.reason: It is not needed once the legal validation frame is retained.

topics.headline: facing image under legal acceptance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that refusal is pictured as not turning toward their speech, while legal acceptance remains the selected sense.
topics.reason: Facing and acceptance belong to the root family, but the local object and prohibition select legal reception or admissibility.

topics.headline: basic reception, not gracious approval
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command concerns admissible reception, not the more gracious acceptance frame seen in other contexts such as 5:27.
topics.reason: The surface is Form I; the 5:27 comparison is a useful contrast but not the governing local register.

topics.headline: testimony made inadmissible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second sanction removes legal validation from the accusers’ testimony.
topics.reason: The verb governs testimony as object and a dative pronoun phrase for the party whose testimony is refused.

words.gloss_range: dative preposition marking the accusers as the party whose testimony-capacity is refused
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) opens a dependent pronoun phrase that keeps the accusers personally attached to the testimony ban. The relation can be heard as for them, from them, or belonging to them, but the local payoff is sharper: their own admissible speech is what the ruling removes. Its placement before the testimony noun keeps the disqualified persons in view first.

topics.headline: accusers marked as testimony source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the testimony ban is personally attached to the accusers as the source of the disqualified speech.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the pronoun and marks the party whose testimony is refused before the testimony object is named.

words.gloss_range: third-person plural pronoun resuming the accuser group inside the testimony-ban phrase
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) completes the dative phrase and points back to the same accusers. The verse can therefore move from flog them, to do not accept testimony for them, to those are the boundary-exiters without reopening the class description. The pronoun chain makes the penalties accumulate on one group.

topics.headline: prior-community note adds no separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The 24:3 community note is too brief to add a separate payoff beyond the retained pronoun-chain continuity.
topics.reason: It does not change the antecedent relation in the local clause.

topics.headline: one group through all penalties
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one accused group is carried through flogging, testimony rejection, and the final verdict.
topics.reason: The pronoun is definite by reference and resumes the relative-headed accuser group.

words.gloss_range: indefinite testimony act under prohibition, universalizing inadmissibility and echoing the earlier witness-agent demand
words.root_gloss_range: presence, witnessing, attestation, and testimony; local verbal noun names testimony as an act or capacity
words.prose: {{ar:شَهَٰدَةً}} ({{tr:shahādatan}}) names the testimony act that is no longer admissible. Because it is indefinite under prohibition, the ban reaches any testimony from them, not only testimony about the original accusation. The same root had just named the demanded witness-agents, so failure to produce witnessing becomes loss of testimony-capacity.

topics.headline: creedal and martyrdom senses not active
topics.blocking_evidence: The local object of the acceptance verb is legal testimony, and no local evidence activates creedal declaration or martyrdom as operative senses.
topics.reason: The broader polysemy should not replace the legal testimony sense selected by the clause.

topics.headline: next-ayah phrase note is duplicate
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The brief next-ayah pointer does not add a separate word-level payoff here.
topics.reason: The phrase note is already represented by the universal testimony-ban topic and the following time-adverb word.

topics.headline: witness agents become lost testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof they failed to supply returns as the very capacity they lose.
topics.reason: The root appears first as demanded witness-agents and then as the testimony-act object of refusal.

topics.headline: any testimony made inadmissible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sanction reaches testimony generally from the accusers, not only the disputed case.
topics.reason: The testimony noun is an indefinite direct object under the prohibition.

words.gloss_range: accusative temporal adverb extending the testimony prohibition across future time
words.root_gloss_range: unbounded duration, foreverness, and continuing time; local adverb scopes over the no-acceptance command
words.prose: {{ar:أَبَدًۭا}} ({{tr:abadan}}) gives the testimony ban explicit temporal reach. As an accusative adverb, it modifies the non-acceptance command rather than floating as an abstract idea of eternity. Inside 24:4 the ban has no internal sunset; 24:5 then supplies the controlled exception route, so the permanence is established before its repair is named. Its later use in 24:17 links legal disqualification with never returning to such speech, while duration contexts such as 4:57, 18:3, and 72:23 show strength of duration without making this legal penalty eschatological.

topics.headline: tanwin cadence duplicate
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The cadence point repeats the retained testimony-plus-duration payoff.
topics.reason: The cadence point is already covered by the testimony-plus-duration unit in the temporal-scope topic.

topics.headline: duration echoes without equivalence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the adverb carries strong duration across contexts, including 24:17, while legal disqualification should not be equated with eschatological duration.
topics.reason: The 24:17 recurrence and other duration contexts show semantic weight, but they do not make this legal penalty identical to paradise or hell duration.

topics.headline: permanence before 24:5 repair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 24:4 first states an unsunsetted ban, while 24:5 controls how repair can enter.
topics.reason: The adverb is absolute inside this ayah, but the next ayah creates an exception route that must qualify commentary on permanence.

topics.headline: forever scopes over prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that permanence is grammatical scope over the testimony prohibition, not a free-standing flourish.
topics.reason: The word is an accusative time adverb modifying the acceptance prohibition.

words.gloss_range: final connector adding and possibly resuming the closing nominal verdict
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links the final verdict to the penalty sequence while letting it stand as a fresh nominal judgment. The ayah has moved from bodily penalty to testimony ban; this connector carries the sequence into identity classification. The result is cumulative and declarative at once.

topics.headline: final verdict linked and resumed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final moral verdict is both attached to the penalties and strong enough to stand as its own clause.
topics.reason: The connector can coordinate the verdict with prior penalties while the demonstrative opens a nominal sentence.

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative pointing back to the accusers as a separated class before the predicate verdict
words.prose: {{ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}) points back to the accusers with distance. The demonstrative gathers the whole prior condition and penalties into a visible class, then prepares the definite predicate equation. Before the label is even spoken, the grammar has set the accusers apart from admissible communal trust.

topics.headline: demonstrative prepares closed predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing clause is an identity equation, not an indefinite description.
topics.reason: The demonstrative subject and definite predicate are joined through the following separator to form a closed verdict.

topics.headline: accusers pointed out at distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusers are grammatically set apart before the final label names them.
topics.reason: The demonstrative points back to the relative-described accusers and uses distal deixis in the legal coda.

words.gloss_range: separating pronoun tightening the nominal verdict into an emphatic identity equation
words.prose: {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) locks the demonstrative and predicate together. As a separating pronoun, it marks the final word as predicate and strengthens the equation: those very accusers are the named class. The closing is therefore not merely that they acted badly, but that the verdict identifies their standing.

topics.headline: plural bridge across the coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same plural accuser group remains locked across demonstrative, separator, and predicate.
topics.reason: Plural agreement and independent pronoun form bridge the subject and predicate without creating a new referent.

topics.headline: emphatic identity separator
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coda asserts identity-status rather than narrating another action.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun sits between demonstrative subject and definite predicate as a separating pronoun.

words.gloss_range: definite active participle predicate naming the accusers as the recognized boundary-exiting class
words.root_gloss_range: exiting, breaking out, and moral-legal transgression; local participle names a durable agentive class
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ}} ({{tr:al-fāsiqūna}}) lands as the ayah's categorical coda. The definite active participle names a recognized class, not just a one-time act, and the plural predicate seals the sequence as a class verdict. The root's boundary-exit image reverses the attempted breach: the protected women remain guarded while the accusers are named as those outside moral-legal standing. Later use at 24:55 shows the same root marking communal exclusion in another register.

topics.headline: brief transition rows duplicate retained frame
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The brief adjacent-ayah notes duplicate the retained coda and boundary-frame topics.
topics.reason: The brief adjacent-ayah notes do not add beyond the retained coda and boundary-frame topics.

topics.headline: wider category without flattening local verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the label belongs to a wider Quranic category, including 24:55, while this verse applies it specifically to failed accusers.
topics.reason: Cross-references show a broader category of boundary violation, but the local predicate is fixed on the qadhf accusers.

topics.headline: plural coda seals the sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final plural predicate audibly and structurally seals the penalty sequence as a class verdict.
topics.reason: The word closes the ayah after the three-part consequence chain.

topics.headline: protected target and boundary-exiter reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reversal: the accusers try to breach protected status, but the closing root says they are the ones outside the boundary.
topics.reason: The root image of exiting a boundary forms a frame with the earlier protected-object word.

topics.headline: recognized transgressor class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word classifies the accusers as a recognized standing category, not merely as people who committed an isolated act.
topics.reason: The word is definite, nominative, active participle predicate in the closing nominal sentence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction يَرْمُونَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتِ joins ر م ي at word 2 to ح ص ن at word 3.
baseline_models.mechanism: The accusation is a launched verbal object aimed at a person held within a protective enclosure; without proof, the utterance functions as an attack on that enclosure rather than as neutral information.

activation_trace.role: Verbal casting supplies the projectile motion and makes the allegation the attacking object.
Protection inside a surrounding fort supplies the social boundary at which the verbal projectile is aimed.
Guarded sexual integrity identifies what the enclosing protection preserves.

changed_reading.before: The ayah merely penalizes a false sexual accusation.
changed_reading.after: The ayah treats unsupported accusatory speech as a projectile that attempts to breach another person's protected sexual and social boundary.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ anchors proof in ء ت ي, ر ب ع, and ش ه د at words 6-8.
baseline_models.mechanism: A projected assertion must be displaced by brought, fourfold, presence-based knowledge: arrival and witnessed disclosure convert speech into admissible proof.

activation_trace.role: Bringing or presenting something supplies the required movement of evidence into the forum.
The literal count of four fixes the multiplicity required before the claim may cross the proof threshold.
Presence with direct observation supplies the epistemic quality required of the four.
Knowledge-bearing declaration supplies both the demanded proof and the later testimony that is refused.

changed_reading.before: Four witnesses are an unexplained numerical prerequisite.
changed_reading.after: The fourfold requirement is a conversion gate: a thrown claim must become multiply present, knowledge-bearing testimony before it can act on the accused.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The consequences run through ج ل د at words 9 and 11, ق ب ل at 13, ء ب د at 16, and ف س ق at 19.
baseline_models.mechanism: The response moves across nested boundaries: the accuser's bodily surface is struck, the institutional gate stops receiving the accuser's speech, and the accuser is named as having exited the containing norm.

activation_trace.role: The skin as bodily covering supplies the surface to which the consequence returns.
Striking the skin supplies the first and bodily layer of the response.
Reception with assent supplies the institutional gate now closed to the accuser's testimony.
Enduring duration makes the refusal prospective rather than confined to the present case.
A date leaving its rind supplies the image of exit from a containing moral order.

changed_reading.before: Flogging, rejected testimony, and the label fasiq are three separate penalties.
changed_reading.after: They form a boundary-restoration sequence: bodily consequence, quarantine of future speech, and classification of the unsupported thrower as outside the norm that makes testimony trustworthy.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening declaration of a specifically delimited obligation and the adjacent use of the same skin-strike lexeme for a proven act place 24:4 inside a calibrated proof-and-sanction regime, not an eruption of private retaliation.

activation_trace.role: The focus supplies a measured striking of the skin as the consequence for an unsupported accusation.
A bounded obligation with a known limit makes the ensuing sanctions formally specified measures.
The same striking image, set at one hundred for the established act, provides the comparison that calibrates the focus's eighty.
Public presence at the preceding punishment distinguishes witnessed adjudication from rumor-driven injury.

structural_cues: 24:1 calls the surah imposed and clear; 24:2 uses the same ج ل د verb-noun pair for one hundred strokes and requires a witnessing group before 24:4 assigns eighty to unsupported accusation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delimited obligation, parallel measured striking, and public presence; I infer a calibrated legal architecture. A live alternative is that the juxtaposed penalties are independent commands whose numerical relation should not itself be interpreted.

changed_reading.before: The eighty strokes look like an isolated retaliation for insulting speech.
changed_reading.after: The eighty belong to a public, measured regime that differentiates punishment of a proved sexual act from punishment of an accusation that failed its proof gate.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate turn to active repair and protective forgiveness prevents أَبَدًا and فَاسِقُونَ from flattening every consequence into an irreparable identity: moral exit can be repaired even while the duration of testimonial exclusion remains a live question.

activation_trace.role: Long duration supplies the apparently permanent horizon of refused testimony.
Exit from a rind supplies the damaged moral location that the next ayah may address.
Removing estrangement between people makes reform an active repair of the social damage, not only inward remorse.
Covering the fault and protecting its bearer from its effect supplies the possibility of restored moral standing.

structural_cues: 24:5 begins with an immediate exception, joins repentance to subsequent reform, and closes with forgiveness and mercy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exception after the three consequences plus repair and protective covering; I infer that the fasiq classification is not an immutable essence. The materially live alternative is that the exception also lifts the perpetual testimony bar, rather than repairing only moral status.

changed_reading.before: Never accepting testimony and naming the accuser fasiq make every consequence permanently irreversible.
changed_reading.after: The ayah fixes a grave prospective disability, but the next ayah opens a repair path for moral and social standing; exactly how far that exception reaches remains unresolved.

context_deltas.mechanism: Where the alleged event is enclosed within marriage and external witnesses are unavailable, the surah preserves the fourfold form by multiplying the spouse's own testimony, then adds a fifth self-exposing invocation and a mirrored counter-testimony.

activation_trace.role: The focus supplies the ordinary demand for four knowledge-bearing declarations and the later admissibility consequence.
The marital pair defines the exceptional intimate domain in which four external observers are structurally unavailable.
The person's own self supplies the substituted witnessing locus.
Repeated declaration turns a single spouse's assertion into a formally exposed testimonial sequence.
The literal four is retained even when four distinct witnesses are not.
Mutual imprecation supplies the fifth, self-endangering seal on the substituted testimony.
The accused spouse's mirrored declarations make the procedure reciprocal and capable of averting punishment.

structural_cues: 24:6-9 replace four outside witnesses with four declarations plus a fifth invocation, then mirror that sequence for the accused spouse.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies marital enclosure, self as sole witness, repeated fourfold testimony, a fifth imprecation, and reciprocal defense; I infer a controlled substitution rather than a relaxation of proof. The live alternative is to treat this as a wholly separate oath procedure with no conceptual revision of 24:4 beyond its explicit exception.

changed_reading.before: The focus seems to require four separate witnesses without qualification whenever such an accusation is voiced.
changed_reading.after: Four remains the normal public proof gate, but intimate inaccessibility receives a tightly structured substitute that multiplies and endangers self-testimony rather than licensing a bare accusation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later false report is turned away from truth, held and amplified by an encircling group, poured outward, caught as taught speech by tongues, emitted through mouths, and diffused socially. The focus's verbal throw therefore includes a relay process in which reception without knowledge becomes renewed projection.

activation_trace.role: Verbal casting anchors every later transmission stage back to the focus's accusatory act.
Turning a thing away from its direction gives the report its initial reversal away from truth.
An encircling, mutually supporting group supplies the social carrier that gives the report collective force.
Speech spreading like overflow supplies the transition from bounded allegation to uncontrolled circulation.
Taking and passing on taught speech supplies the receiving relay rather than firsthand observation.
The tongue as speech-organ becomes the hand that catches and throws the report onward.
The mouth as an outlet supplies the report's point of re-emission despite absent knowledge.
Diffusion and dispersal supply the network-scale harm produced by repeated verbal throws.

structural_cues: 24:11 locates the falsehood in a group, 24:14 names communal overflow into it, 24:15 describes tongue-to-tongue reception without knowledge, and 24:19 names desired diffusion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a group, overflow, speech reception, tongue and mouth transfer, and diffusion; I infer that each relay functionally renews the focus's throw. A live alternative is that only the originator is legally a thrower while relayers incur a different, though related, blame.

changed_reading.before: The focus addresses one accuser making one damaging statement.
changed_reading.after: The focus also operates as transmission control: an unsupported accusation is a relay projectile, and those who catch and resend it help breach the protected person's enclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later near-repetition turns failure to present the four from a mere evidentiary shortfall into a status reversal: the claimants, not the accused, are placed on the side of falsehood.

activation_trace.role: The repeated literal four identifies the same threshold as the focus.
Directly present observers supply the missing basis against which the circulated allegation is tested.
Failure to bring the witnesses makes the threshold failure an enacted absence, not a merely incomplete argument.
Attributing falsehood to a person supplies the explicit reversal of status onto the unsupported claimants.

structural_cues: 24:13 repeats four witnesses and the failure to bring them, then concludes that the speakers are the liars before God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit if-not-brought-then-liars sequence; I infer an operative presumption that protects the accused in public adjudication. A live alternative is that the conclusion states divine moral status without claiming that every unsupported allegation is privately known to be factually impossible.

changed_reading.before: Failure to produce four witnesses merely means that the accusation cannot be proved.
changed_reading.after: Within the surah's public truth regime, the failure reverses the burden decisively: the unproved accusers acquire the falsehood status they tried to attach to the protected person.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated throw targets protected women who were outside anticipatory suspicion, but the accusers' own speaking and acting organs later supply the testimony they failed to bring, while the targets are separated from what was said about them.

activation_trace.role: The repeated verbal accusation carries the focus act into the later witness scene.
Guarded sexual integrity repeats the focus's protected target.
Being outside alert suspicion makes the targets unprepared for attack and intensifies the asymmetry of the throw.
Present witnessing returns, now directed against those who lacked witnesses for their accusation.
The same organ that emitted or relayed speech becomes an involuntary witness to its use.
Hands bearing what they earned extend testimony from words to accountable action.
The bodily foot completes the conversion of the accuser's own embodied conduct into evidence.
Separation and freedom from attachment release the targets from the sayings projected onto them.
Spoken output identifies the material from which the protected people are finally separated.

structural_cues: 24:23 repeats the focus's accusers and protected women; 24:24 makes tongues, hands, and feet testify against the accusers; 24:26 declares others clear of what they say.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated accusation, unsuspecting protected targets, organ-witnesses, and separation from the sayings; I infer a deliberate weapon-to-witness reversal. A live alternative is that the eschatological testimony supplements the temporal rule without defining its legal mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The witness requirement ends when the accuser fails to prove the charge and receives temporal penalties.
changed_reading.after: The witness motif reverses: the speech-organ that launched the unproved charge eventually testifies against its user, while the accused is detached from the projected saying.

context_deltas.mechanism: Rules for houses, permission, retreat, restrained sight, guarded openings, and covering turn the focus's حصن from a static honor label into a consent-governed access system. Reputation and sexual privacy become protected interiors that observation or speech may not enter unlicensed.

activation_trace.role: The focus supplies an enclosing fort as the anchor for the later access-control pattern.
Movement into an interior supplies the kind of boundary crossing that requires authorization.
A dwelling as shelter supplies the concrete protected interior parallel to حصن.
Permission supplies the positive condition for legitimate access.
Required return supplies the response when access is refused.
Withholding and lowering perception limits the first stage from which intimate claims might arise.
Eye-seeing supplies the sensory channel that must itself respect the protected boundary.
Preserving sexual sanctity and covenant supplies an active guarding practice rather than a passive status.
Covering supplies a material instance of controlled visibility within the wider privacy system.

structural_cues: 24:27-28 prohibit entering another's house without authorization and command retreat when refused; 24:30-31 govern sight, sexual guarding, visibility, and covering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a focus fort plus later protocols for interior access, perception, guarding, and covering; I infer that protected reputation is organized like consent-governed space. A live alternative is that these are parallel privacy rules and should not be made a lexical gloss of مُحْصَنَات.

changed_reading.before: The protected women are bearers of a fixed chastity or status predicate.
changed_reading.after: They also stand at the center of an access architecture: intimate interiority, sight, and reputation are guarded domains, and unsupported accusation is an unauthorized verbal entry.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later use of تحصن as something desired by women being forced into sexual exploitation makes حصن an active claim to bodily protection under coercion, not merely proof of marriage, social rank, or an uncontested past.

activation_trace.role: Guarded sexual integrity anchors the later coercion scene directly to the focus's protected target.
Refraining from what should be avoided supplies active self-restraint as a practice of protection.
Among the indexed uses, the sexual-exploitation sense names the commerce into which the women are being forced.
Compelling another to what she rejects assigns the boundary violation to the coercer.
Desired sexual guarding makes حصن an asserted protective orientation even under vulnerable conditions.

structural_cues: 24:33 prohibits forcing vulnerable women into sexual exploitation when they desire تحصن and places forgiveness after their coercion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies self-restraint, forced exploitation, and desired تحصن; I infer that the focus protects an agency-bearing boundary even where social power is unequal. A live alternative is that the focus's participle has a narrower conventional status while 24:33's verbal noun describes a context-specific aspiration.

changed_reading.before: مُحْصَنَات may be heard mainly as women whose established marital or social status guarantees respectability.
changed_reading.after: The surah's own reuse of حصن extends the protective logic to vulnerable women actively seeking sexual integrity under coercion, preventing exploitation from being converted into blame against them.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later contrasts between accepting judgment and approaching only when the outcome favors oneself recast testimonial acceptance as participation in a reciprocal trust order. The unsupported accuser loses that privilege because the accusation attempted to make public judgment work one way.

activation_trace.role: Receiving testimony with institutional assent supplies the civic privilege placed in question.
Exit from a containing rind supplies exclusion from the norm that sustains reciprocal adjudication.
Judgment between people supplies the reciprocal forum in which testimony must function.
Fear of partiality identifies the forum's central risk: judgment bent toward one party.
Hearing as understanding and compliance supplies willingness to receive judgment rather than only to speak into it.
Submission supplies reciprocal acceptance of the forum's outcome.
Trust and security supply the social condition that reliable testimony helps maintain.
The repeated exit image places fasiq language at the breakdown of a promised secure order.

structural_cues: 24:47-51 contrast verbal profession with refusal of judgment and selective compliance; 24:55 joins trust, security, and a renewed fasiq classification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies judgment, fear of partiality, hearing-as-compliance, trust-security, and repeated fasiq language; I infer that refusing an accuser's future testimony protects reciprocal civic trust. A live alternative is that the later judgment passage concerns obedience generally and does not specify the institutional rationale of 24:4.

changed_reading.before: Permanent rejection of testimony is chiefly a stigma attached to the offender.
changed_reading.after: It also functions as a trust quarantine: someone who tried to weaponize adjudication without its proof discipline is denied future power to make that institution act on another's word.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because ثَمَانِينَ is plainly the numeral eighty, while the value branch of ث م ن is form-distant; it remains anchored in that exact focus root and the measured skin penalty. Downstream prose should present a counter-price resonance, never replace the literal number or claim an etymological derivation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ث م ن at word 10 stands between the absent four witnesses and the counted skin strikes.

activation_trace.role: The missing literal four supplies the evidentiary quantity against which the sanction is set.
Value or exchange supplies an exploratory sense of a costly counter-price for devaluing protected reputation.
Counted striking of the skin makes that counter-price bodily and publicly exacted.

changed_reading.before: Eighty is only the fixed quantity of the sanction.
changed_reading.after: Alongside its literal count, eighty can faintly resonate as a bodily counter-price imposed when unsupported speech tries to spend another person's protected reputation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The cord and shared-load images are surprising because أَرْبَعَة is functioning as an ordinary numeral; they remain anchored to the exact four-witness construction and illuminate multiplicity without altering it. Render only as a structural analogy for corroboration, not as the lexical meaning of the verse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ر ب ع at word 7 directly qualifies the witnesses whose presence must support the claim.

activation_trace.role: A cord twisted on four strengths supplies an image of proof that gains integrity from independent strands.
Several participants lifting a load supplies an image of distributed evidentiary burden.
Directly present observers keep the cord-and-load analogy tied to actual witnessing.

changed_reading.before: Four witnesses are simply four interchangeable units.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the four act like independent strands or co-bearers: the accusation cannot carry public weight unless corroboration distributes and stabilizes its load.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain optics model is surprising because 24:39-40 concern mirage and darkness rather than accusation; it remains anchored in the focus's branch of mistaken projection and its demand for observed testimony. Downstream prose should mark it as an epistemic analogy, not a legal definition of witnessing.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ر م ي at word 2 includes mistaken conjectural casting, while ش ه د at words 8 and 15 demands presence and observation.

activation_trace.role: Casting an inaccurate conjecture anchors the accusation in mistaken projection rather than verified perception.
Presence with observation supplies the focus's answer to projection.
A mirage gleaming like water supplies the image of an appearance that invites a confident but false claim.
Conjectural reckoning supplies the observer's mistaken conversion of seeming into fact.
Arriving and failing to find the expected object tests and dissolves the projection.
Failure of eye-seeing in layered darkness supplies the opposite limit: an appearance claim without adequate visibility.

changed_reading.before: Unsupported accusation is simply a lie or an unproved report.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it is also mirage-speech: conjecture hardens a seeming into public fact, while fourfold witnessed presence demands that the claim survive shared visibility.

strongest_changes: The four-witness threshold became both a public truth-status switch and, in the spousal case, a tightly controlled fourfold oath substitution.
ر م ي expanded from one speaker's verbal attack into a relay projectile propagated by group support, overflow, tongues, mouths, and diffusion.
ح ص ن shifted from a static respectability label toward consent-governed protection that remains meaningful for vulnerable women under coercion.
The bodily, testimonial, and fasiq consequences became a calibrated trust-restoration sequence, with the next ayah preserving a live path of moral repair.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context repeatedly reused the focus's roots while surrounding them with rumor transmission, privacy, coercion, adjudication, and witness reversal, producing mechanisms unavailable to a focus-only reading.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact scope of 24:5's exception over the perpetual testimony bar versus the fasiq classification remains grammatically live.
The spousal oath sequence clearly substitutes a special procedure, but how much it conceptually revises the ordinary four-witness rule remains open.
The enclosure, counter-price, four-strand, and mirage models are anchored analogies; none should displace the direct legal and lexical senses.
ح ص ن remains multivalent across chastity, marriage, status, and active self-protection, and the packet does not force those senses into one gloss.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Accusation is a projectile aimed at a fortified social body.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ر م ي` B001 is physical casting/shooting and B008 accusatory speech; `ح ص ن` B001 is guarding within a fortified enclosure and B002 chastity as guarded sexuality; `ش ه د` B002 is testimony from knowledge. **Structural cue:** the ayah first “throws,” then requires four witnesses to be brought, then redirects skin-striking and testimonial exclusion onto the unsupported thrower; 24:6-8 likewise make testimony, not allegation, the operative legal instrument. **Assigned role:** the projectile branch models the accusation's capacity to breach another's protection, while the witness threshold functions as the gate that must authorize penetration of that enclosure. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies projectile, fortification, evidence, and reversal of consequence; I infer accusation → attempted breach, with failed proof → consequence rebounding to the thrower. **Reading change:** slander becomes an assault with directional force, not harmless speech awaiting correction.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:6-8 sharpened the projectile image by showing what a licensed evidentiary route looks like; repeated accountable testimony, not forceful accusation, can cross the protected boundary.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A norm becomes effective by being bounded, placed, counted, witnessed, and finally registered at its proper moral magnitude.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Lexical branches make legislation spatial and corporeal: a surah resembles an enclosing wall, obligation a scored cut, punishment a measured impact on skin, and culpability an allocated share whose apparent and actual sizes diverge.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Counted Impact on Skin
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Exact quantities terminate in a bodily surface where the sanction is materially received.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: bodily skin or hide `quranic:root_000253:B001/m01`; striking that reaches the skin `quranic:root_000253:B004/m01`; completion to one hundred `quranic:root_001394:B002/m01`; eight as the numerical base of eighty `quranic:root_000206:B002/m01`; numerical oneness `quranic:root_001631:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Number and body form one scene rather than two adjacent topics. The count fixes the sanction's extent, while the skin branch identifies its receiving boundary. The latent craft sense of exact completion pressures any reading that would dissolve the stated quantities into an unbounded response.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Ordinary Witness Threshold
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A charge crosses into adjudicable knowledge only when a fixed number of present observers can articulate it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: presence with direct observation `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; testimony that declares known fact `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; the witness as an articulating tongue `quranic:root_000822:B005/m01`; the number four `quranic:root_000536:B001/m01`; bounded individual unit `quranic:root_001631:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Presence, knowledge, articulation, and count cooperate as a single evidentiary gate. A claim does not become proof merely by circulation; four embodied positions must convert observation into public declaration.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P1 24:1-20] Speech Moves as a Physical Force
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: An utterance can be launched, received, relayed, spilled, and intensified; social speech therefore behaves like force moving through material media.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The network materializes accusation as projectile injury and rumor as both fluid overflow and fire propagation, exposing distinct mechanisms rather than one generic “speech” domain.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Accusation as Projectile Injury
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A verbal charge is launched toward a protected target, reaches listeners through abusive sound, and leaves a wound-like mark.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: launching an object `quranic:root_000603:B001/m01`; projectile, point, or struck quarry `quranic:root_000603:B003/m01`; verbal accusation `quranic:root_000603:B008/m01`; inaccurate shot of judgment `quranic:root_000603:B009/m01`; shield or practice target `quranic:root_000466:B005/m01`; abusive speech made audible `quranic:root_000741:B006/m01`; bodily wound `quranic:root_001316:B003/m01`; taking or attacking someone by the tongue `quranic:root_001355:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The charge inherits the mechanics of a shot: projection, target, possible mis-aim, reception, and injury. The protected person is not merely discussed but struck in a social body, while the tongue functions as the attacking instrument and hearing as the point of impact.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P1 24:1-20] Reputation Has an Enclosure, Breach, and Repair
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Sexual reputation is treated as an inhabited protected interior whose boundary can be crossed, whose covering can split, and whose integrity can be restored.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Fort, precinct, shell, cover, and wound-relapse senses turn abstract honor into boundary maintenance and make repentance a practical reconstruction rather than a merely verbal reversal.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Fortified Chastity
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Chastity occupies a defended interior protected by fortification, inviolable precinct, and covering.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: preservation inside an encircling fort `quranic:root_000331:B001/m01`; guarded sexual integrity `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`; inviolable precinct and its protected margin `quranic:root_000313:B003/m01`; protected right or sanctity `quranic:root_000313:B006/m01`; a cover that shields what is beneath it `quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The protected woman and the protected claim about her become one fortified scene. Chastity is an interior condition, prohibition marks its perimeter, and covering prevents destructive exposure. The spatial model explains why unsupported accusation is treated as boundary violation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P1 24:1-20] Reputation Has an Enclosure, Breach, and Repair
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Sexual reputation is treated as an inhabited protected interior whose boundary can be crossed, whose covering can split, and whose integrity can be restored.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Shell-Break and Exposure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Obscene speech crosses a fixed perimeter and forces what was enclosed outward, like fruit breaking through its husk.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: exceeding a proper limit `quranic:root_001134:B002/m01`; obscene speech or action `quranic:root_001134:B003/m01`; a ripe date exiting its shell `quranic:root_001156:B002/m01`; false charge that stuns its target or hearer `quranic:root_000157:B002/m01`; the protected sexual interior `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Transgression is rendered as forced emergence through a protective casing. The husk image makes `فسق` a structural exit, while obscene and stunning speech enact the pressure that breaches the enclosure. The result is exposure, not just doctrinal error.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Sexual accusation reaches beyond an isolated act into pairing, marital legitimacy, conception, gestation, birth, and the traces by which lineage becomes socially visible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Womb, postpartum blood, afterbirth, birth witness, midwife, and rapid conception branches disclose the lineage stakes that make sexual testimony unusually consequential.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Pairing, Contract, and Sexual Contact
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Two persons are paired through a recognized marital relation whose protected interior includes sexual contact.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: spouse in a marital pair `quranic:root_000652:B002/m01`; joining one thing as the mate of another `quranic:root_000652:B003/m01`; sexual intercourse `quranic:root_001548:B001/m01`; marriage contract `quranic:root_001548:B002/m01`; marriage as a protecting status `quranic:root_000331:B003/m01`; sexual contact `quranic:root_001423:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Contract, pairing, protected status, and bodily contact form one social-reproductive frame. The latent sexual sense of touch at 24:14 does not replace the surface meaning of affliction; it resonates with the marital field already active and sharpens what an accusation puts at risk.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Gestation and Birth Leave Evidence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A womb receives conception, carries a child, releases birth material, and is attended by recognizable traces and a receiving agent.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: womb as the child's growing enclosure `quranic:root_000552:B003/m01`; pregnancy and postpartum emergence `quranic:root_001533:B005/m01`; blood or membrane accompanying birth as a witness `quranic:root_000822:B006/m01`; afterbirth and uterine discharge `quranic:root_000994:B009/m01`; midwife receiving the newborn `quranic:root_001198:B007/m01`; rapid conception `quranic:root_001372:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The branch network assembles a complete reproductive sequence from roots otherwise active in mercy, selfhood, witness, punishment, reception, and verbal relay. This scene usefully reframes why proof rules guard lineage: birth itself yields bodily witnesses, while rumor tries to manufacture social evidence without them.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir nesneyi elden bırakıp uzağa göndermeyi temel alıyor; ok, taş, hedef ve av örnekleri bu fiziksel atma çekirdeğinin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

concept_map.definition: Bir nesneyi elden çıkararak uzağa ya da belirli bir hedefe doğru göndermektir. Okla atış, karşılıklı atışma ve hedefe veya ava çıkma bu çekirdeğin biçime bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sanıya dayalı yargıyı ve bu yargının isabetsiz oluşunu birlikte karşılar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Doğrulanmamış ve sonuçta yanlış çıkan bir sanıyı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Şüphenin giderildiği, bilginin sağlam ve kesin olduğu durumu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal bir yargının bilgi ve doğruluk bakımından taşıdığı güven düzeyini karşılaştırır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal isabetsiz sanı kutbunda, komşu dal ise şüphenin kalktığı kesin bilgi kutbunda yer alır; ortak eksen yargının doğrulanma ve güven derecesidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, çevresi sağlamlaştırılmış ve içine erişim engellenmiş yeri merkeze alır; korumaya alma, korunma ve sığınma biçimleri de bu mekansal çekirdekten türemektedir. Köy ve zırh örnekleri ayrı birer çekirdek değil, aynı çevreleyici korumanın özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, cinsel sakınmayı ya da evlilik durumunu değil, çevreleyen bir engelle sağlanan somut veya genişletilmiş korumayı kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, ad ve türemiş eylem biçimlerini birlikte kapsar; köy ve zırh gibi yapıya bağlı kullanımlar kendi bağlamlarında tutulur ve yalın köke genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir yerin çevresinin sağlam bir engelle kuşatılması, içine erişimin güçleştirilmesi ve içerideki kişi ya da şeyin korunmasıdır. Türemiş kullanımlar, böyle bir korunak oluşturmayı, ona çekilerek korunmayı veya daha genel olarak tehlikeden sakınmayı anlatır; köy ve zırh örnekleri bu çekirdeğin özel uygulamalarıdır.

facets.statement: Çevreleyen sağlam engel, içeriye erişimi keser ve içeride bulunanı dış tehlikeden korur.
Türemiş eylem biçimleri bir yeri korunaklı kılmayı, kişinin korunaklı yere çekilip korunmasını veya daha genel olarak tehlikeden sakınmasını anlatır.
Çevresi sağlamlaştırılmış köy ile bedeni koruyan sık dokunmuş zırh, çevreleyici korumanın yapıya bağlı örnekleridir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği koruma, çevreleme ve erişimi önleyen sağlam engeldir. Somut savunmalı yer bu çekirdeği doğrudan taşırken, bir yeri korunaklı kılma, korunaklı yere çekilme ve daha genel olarak tehlikeden sakınma aynı yapının türemiş görünümleridir; sağlam köy ve koruyucu zırh ise özelleşmiş örnekleridir.

concept_gloss.text: korunaklı çevre, onu kurma, ona sığınma ve genel olarak sakınma
concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın yer, korunak oluşturma, korunak içinde güvene çekilme ve daha genel olarak tehlikeden sakınma yönlerini birlikte gösteren üst düzey karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Çevreleyen engeli, içeriye erişimin kesilmesini, koruma sonucunu, bu korunağı kurma ya da ona çekilme yönlerini ve genel sakınma uzantısını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İçine erişimin sağlam bir çevreyle engellendiği somut yer adlandırılırken doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: İçeridekini dışarıdan koruyan ve erişimi güçleştiren yer sonucunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Korunağı kurma, ona çekilme ve zırh gibi özel uygulamaları tek başına anlatmaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir yerin çevresine koruyucu yapı kurarak onu erişilmesi güç hale getirme eyleminde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Korunak oluşturma işlemini ve bu işlemle sağlanan korumayı korur.
error_profile.loses: Ortaya çıkan yer adını ve kişinin korunaklı yere çekilmesi yönünü kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişi ya da topluluğun saldırıdan sakınmak için koruyucu bir yere sığınmasını anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Koruyucu çevreden yararlanarak güvene geçme ve erişimi engelleme yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Korunağın inşa edilmesini ve somut korunak adını doğrudan anlatmaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Koruyucu çevre işlevinin bedeni saran sağlam zırhla gerçekleştiği özel kullanım içindir.

error_profile.preserves: Sağlam bir dış katmanın içerideki bedeni koruması yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Yer, yapı kurma ve korunaklı yere çekilme yönlerini kapsamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, savunmalı yerin yanında korunak oluşturma, ona çekilme ve zırh gibi özel uzantıları da içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, savunma yapılarıyla birlikte kişinin korunmak için yararlandığı her türlü aracı daha açık biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da dış erişimi engelleyen bir yapı veya araç sayesinde korunma sağlanır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın çekirdeği çevresi sağlamlaştırılmış yer ve bu korunağı kurma ya da kullanma örüntüsüdür; komşu dal ise korunmak ve direnmek için kullanılan savunma araçları sınıfına daha doğrudan yönelir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalda koruma, çevreleyen sağlam bir yer veya katmanla ve içeriye erişimin engellenmesiyle kurulur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, mekansal çevre gerektirmeden engelleme, tutma, kötülüğü savma ve bir şeye dayanarak korunma eylemlerine uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir tehlikeyi uzak tutarak kişi ya da şeyi koruma sonucunda buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal çevreleyen korunağı kurucu unsur sayar; komşu dalda ise genel engelleme ve kötülüğü savma yeterlidir, kapalı veya sağlamlaştırılmış bir yer gerekmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, savunma sağlayan sağlam çevreyi ve bu çevrenin içine erişilememesini öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, bir şeyi örterek, kap içine alarak veya gözden saklayarak koruma yönünü öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir dış katman ya da kapalı alan, içindeki şeyi zarardan uzak tutar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın ayırt edici yanı savunmalı çevre ve erişim engelidir; komşu dalın ayırt edici yanı örtme, gizleme ve bir kap içinde saklamadır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal somut ya da benzetmeli bir çevre, yapı veya katmanın içeridekini korumasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, kadının yasak cinsel ilişkiden uzak durarak kendisini ve cinsel organını korumasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal, dışarıdan gelebilecek ihlale karşı bir şeyi korunmuş tutma düşüncesini paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Mekansal veya yapısal koruma odak dalın çekirdeğidir; komşu dal bu koruma örüntüsünü cinsel özdenetim ve davranış alanına taşır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الحصن والحصون والموضع الحصين والقرية المحصنة وكل ما جعل حرزا أو حياطة أو إحكاما أو تحرزا، ومنه حفظ الشيء في موضع حصين والدرع الحصينة
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه خصوص العفة أو التزوج إلا من جهة اشتراكهما في معنى الحفظ
branches.source_phrase_ar: الحفظ والحياطة والحرز (maqayis); الحصن كل موضع حصين لا يوصل إلى ما في جوفه (ayn); حصنت القرية إذا بنيت حولها وتحصن العدو (sihah); يتجوز به في كل تحرز ومنه درع حصينة ومما تحصنون أي تحرزون (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, kadının yasak cinsel ilişkiden uzak durmasını ve cinsel organını korumasını dalın kurucu anlamı olarak açıkça verir. Evlilik yalnız başına bu dalı tanımlamaz; evlilikle doğan hukuki durum ayrı dalda tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, kadın ve cinsel davranış bağlamındaki özdenetimle sınırlıdır; savunma yapısı veya sırf evli olma durumu bu çekirdeğe girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Niteleyici ve eylemsel biçimler ortak cinsel özdenetim çekirdeğinde buluşur; cinsel organı koruma yapısı kendi bağlamında tutulur ve yalın kök anlamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kadının yasak cinsel ilişkiden uzak durarak kendisini ve cinsel organını kuşkudan ve ihlalden korumasıdır. Niteleyici biçimler, bu özdenetimi kalıcı bir kadın niteliği olarak sunar.

facets.statement: Kadın, yasak cinsel ilişkiden uzak durur ve cinsel organını bu tür ilişkiden korur.
Niteleyici biçimler, cinsel davranışta kendini korumayı kadına ait yerleşik bir özellik olarak ifade eder.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, kadının cinsel organını koruyarak yasak ilişkiden uzak durması üzerinde birleşir. Eylem biçimleri bu korunmayı gerçekleştirmeyi, niteleyici biçimler ise aynı davranışsal korunmuşluğu kadının özelliği olarak bildirir.

concept_gloss.text: yasak cinsel ilişkiden uzak durarak kendini koruma
concept_gloss.applicability: Kadının hem davranışsal uzak duruşunu hem de cinsel organını korumasını birlikte anlatan temel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Yasak ilişkiden uzak durmayı, cinsel organı korumayı ve bu özdenetimin kadına ait olmasını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Özdenetimin bir kadın niteliği olarak bildirildiği bağlamlarda doğal bir niteleme sağlar.

error_profile.preserves: Kadını, yasak cinsel ilişkiden uzak duran ve kendisini bu alanda koruyan kişi olarak niteler.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Korumanın tamamlanmış bir eylem olarak cinsel organ üzerinden ifade edildiği cümlelerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Cinsel organı yasak ilişkiden koruma eylemini açıkça korur.
error_profile.loses: Bu davranışın kadına ait sürekli bir nitelik olarak sunulması yönünü taşımaz.

error_profile.loses: Yasak cinsel ilişkiden davranışsal olarak uzak durma ve cinsel organı koruma çekirdeğini siler.
